edges.description: Ligand-independent PDGFRB signaling transforms fibroblasts and promotes growth of mesenchymal cells including blood vessels and smooth muscle.
Hyperactivated ligand-independent NOTCH3(L1519P) signaling elevates PDGFRB expression in fibroblasts, feeding into the PDGFRB signaling axis in infantile myofibromatosis.

edges.description: Clonal myofibroblastic and perivascular mesenchymal proliferation directly produces solitary or multicentric myofibromatosis tumors.
Proliferation of transformed fibroblasts and myofibroblasts forms benign fibrous soft-tissue tumors.
Multifocal myofibroblastic growth in subcutaneous tissue manifests as palpable subcutaneous nodules.
Intraosseous myofibroma growth causes localized bone resorption and osteolytic lesions with sclerotic rims.
Dystrophic calcification develops within proliferating and regressing soft-tissue myofibroma masses.
Disseminated myofibroblastic proliferation in the generalized form infiltrates the myocardium to form cardiac myofibromas.
Visceral myofibroblastic proliferation forms nodular tumor masses in the gastrointestinal tract.
Multicentric visceral myofibroblastic proliferation can involve the central nervous system.

nodes.description: In infantile myofibromatosis 2, the NOTCH3 p.Leu1519Pro (L1519P) variant in the negative regulatory region disrupts normal cell-surface localization, causing mutant receptor accumulation in the endoplasmic reticulum, enhanced S1/S2/S3 proteolytic processing, and hyperactivated ligand-independent Notch3 canonical signaling. Hyperactive NOTCH3(L1519P) signaling directly upregulates PDGFRB expression in fibroblasts, functionally linking NOTCH3 gain of function to the PDGFRB signaling axis in infantile myofibromatosis.

nodes.description: Gain-of-function mutations in the transmembrane, juxtamembrane, and kinase domains of PDGFRB—or increased PDGFRB expression driven by hyperactive NOTCH3 signaling—lead to ligand-independent or enhanced receptor tyrosine kinase activation, transforming fibroblasts and promoting perivascular mesenchymal cell growth (both fibroblast and pericyte are bound in cell_types because the tumor cell of origin spans the perivascular pericyte-to-myofibroblast lineage continuum). In sporadic disease, activating PDGFRB mutations frequently arise as post-zygotic somatic mosaic events, reminiscent of multifocal venous malformations induced by TIE2 mutations.
